long_biography.plain_text:
Road building and civil works form the core of MW Afritec’s business in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Its project history includes highway rehabilitation, port infrastructure, drainage, concrete structures and industrial buildings, alongside metal fabrication, quarrying and equipment services.

Alain Wan has led the Kinshasa company for decades, first as its representative and later as president and chief executive. Under that operating role, MW Afritec delivered projects for public agencies and private clients, including work financed by the World Bank and European Union. That career has kept him at the centre of a multi-disciplinary construction and engineering business.

uncertainties.detail: The name Alain Wan is not unique. The dossier resolves the record to the MW Afritec executive because the input's Congolese nationality aligns with multiple sources combining the exact name, Kinshasa location and same company. The lack of birth details keeps identity confidence below very high.
JICA, the official gazette and a current directory render the name as Alain Wan M. The initial is not expanded because reliable non-controversy sources do not establish the underlying name.

Le Monde directly identifies Wan and Marc Piedboeuf as the owners who developed MW Afritec after Wan received it from his parents. Reliable sources do not disclose Wan's current percentage interest, so the dossier does not assign a stake size or treat all company assets as his personal property.

Marriage / family transfer is directly supported at 92 by Le Monde's report that Wan received the MW Afritec business created by his parents in 1984 and then developed it with Marc Piedboeuf. Inherited and Inherited and expanded are rejected because the report identifies a parental transfer but not inheritance; Self-made — advantaged start is rejected because the transferred company remained the principal wealth-producing platform; Mixed lacks an independently supported second material origin mechanism.

The input's Congolese nationality is consistent with the resolved business identity, but the Kinshasa company location is not sufficient to propose personal residence or birth country. Belgian nationality appears only in excluded controversy-focused reporting and is not proposed here.

Multiple directories and the company LinkedIn page publish mwafritec.com as the corporate domain, but the website was unavailable during this research pass. It is proposed at high rather than very-high confidence.

Allegations, investigations, legal matters, political associations and vessel-specific research are excluded from the dossier and biographies. They are not used to resolve identity or classify wealth.

review.notes:
The MW Afritec executive identity, construction-and-engineering classifications and operator relationship are well supported. Under the amended reasonable-inference policy, wealth origin is Marriage / family transfer because reliable reporting directly states that Wan received the company created by his parents and then developed the family business; the precise transfer instrument and current ownership percentage remain undisclosed. Research remains limited because the common name lacks birth identifiers. Nothing has been compiled, approved or applied.
